solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mind in conflict, worker has admitted

indicators.note: something that has admitted another holds it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a worker bee; bee is the standard crossword worker
a conflict between nations is a war

explanation.surface: A worker under inner turmoil has confessed something on their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' is an imperative here, a warning, not the noun for the intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: As an imperative, 'mind!' and 'beware!' are both warnings to take care.

clue.text: Joking harmful, in time

parts.note: bad means harmful
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Jokes that hurt, landing at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is witty, playful banter, so joking is a fair synonym.

clue.text: The American, for example, more like a film?

definitions.meaning: someone from the West, as an American is
read as ..., 'more western', like a cowboy film

explanation.surface: Asking whether an American is more like a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Western world is a westerner; the whimsical second reading treats it as a comparative of the film genre.

clue.text: Uprising in India, revolting attack

indicators.note: Uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rebellion in India leads to an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the hiding indicator: 'in' marks the hidden DIAR. In a down clue 'Uprising' reads it from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault on a place.

clue.text: Principal US composer's record collections

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy
Charles Ives was an American composer; the 's joins him to what follows

explanation.surface: The main record collections of an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are stored collections of historical records and documents.

clue.text: Wild preteen, daughter showed remorse

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly child and their daughter felt sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges PRETEEN into REPENTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Collection of books written after success, actor did very nicely

indicators.note: written after places the collection of books at the end, behind the other pieces

parts.note: a hit is a success
thesp is short for thespian, an actor
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An actor who wrote his books after a hit did well.
explanation.walkthrough: THESP is short for thespian; OT is the crossword's usual Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the spot is an idiom for being exactly satisfying, i.e. doing very nicely.

clue.text: I found in book a Shakespearean character

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the I goes within the book letters

parts.note: vol, short for volume, is a book

explanation.surface: I discovered a Shakespeare character in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I in VOL; the A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Drink reserved, sin opening it

indicators.note: opening means spreading apart, so the first word is split to take the second

parts.note: shy means reserved
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A shy person, sinfully cracking open a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening it' reads like uncorking the drink, but 'opening' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified Spanish wine, a drink.

clue.text: Country type wandering round top of garden

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
wandering letters stray from their places into a new order
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone strolling around the upper end of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges TYPE to EYPT; 'round' puts it around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Bold racing

explanation.surface: A bold horse charging down the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing is both stylishly daring and moving at a dash, i.e. hurrying.

clue.text: European banks though the responsibility of local council?

indicators.note: to bank something is to flank it on both sides, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
tho is an informal shortening of though

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a European and a council's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Road potholes in Britain are mended by the local council, hence the question-marked definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing holes in road surfaces is a typical job for the local authority's highways department.

clue.text: Christmas book, middle torn out

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is ripped away, like a page torn from the middle

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A Christmas book with its central pages ripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle torn out' removes V, the centre letter of NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for Christmas, familiar from carols.

clue.text: Still to decide where pancake, say, tossed?

explanation.surface: Wondering about the pancake toss outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an unsettled matter is also the literal position of a flipped pancake mid-toss.

clue.text: Writer became aware of bonus: pound!

parts.note: to feel something is to become aware of it; felt is the past tense
a tip is a bonus payment
a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen

explanation.surface: A writer notices a bonus worth a pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is a pen, an instrument that writes.

clue.text: Trencherman, figure on horse running backwards

indicators.note: the horse's running backwards tells us to read the letters in reverse

parts.note: ten is a number, i.e. a figure
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A hearty eater sits on a horse that is running in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running backwards' turns TENNAG around.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencherman is a big eater, and gannet is British slang for a greedy eater.

clue.text: Holiday area spreading disease

indicators.note: a disease spreading suggests its letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An epidemic sweeping through a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is a classic holiday destination for British families.

clue.text: Reference leader of Conservatives in shocking politician

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: dire means dreadful, shocking
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so take the word's first letter

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader referenced within a terrible Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reference' is a noun here: a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory, such as a phone book, is a reference work.

clue.text: Main issue with a will ultimately dependent on terms and conditions?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea
issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A legal matter: a will's terms decide what an heir inherits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terms and conditions' are read as seasons and weather: a school term or season.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seasonal depends on the time of year, i.e. its terms and the prevailing weather conditions.

clue.text: Journalist filing record in terror after revolution

indicators.note: a journalist filing copy takes something in; here the record letters are filed within the others
after a revolution things are overturned, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A journalist reporting on terror after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' paints a political uprising but signals a shuffle: 'after revolution' gives RORTER, and 'filing' takes the record within.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers news.

clue.text: Waste food

definitions.meaning: to ... money or time is to waste it
a piece of fried battered food

explanation.surface: Throwing food away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritter as a verb means squander; as a noun it is a fried, battered snack.

clue.text: No more playing for old player

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters fooling around into a new order

explanation.surface: A veteran sportsman being told his playing days are over.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was a film actress, and a player is an actor.

clue.text: Sailor hat

explanation.surface: A sailor's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Boater means both a person in a boat and a stiff straw hat.

clue.text: "Who" translated on paper

parts.note: qui is French for who
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A quoted question word translated onto paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is a quantity of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets.

clue.text: Paul is too upset about unknown quantity in hot food

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: x is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Paul is distressed about some mysterious amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles PAULISTOO into OTAILSOUP; 'about' puts it around X.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick soup made with beef tail, served hot.

clue.text: Subject matter in photo pictured

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The subject shown in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of discussion.

clue.text: Sound returning ends in one classic match: bravo!

indicators.note: ends in tells us to take the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A cheer echoes around the stadium at the end of a famous game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo!' looks like applause, but it is just the last word supplying its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back to the listener.

clue.text: Figure one: short figurine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a doll is a small figure

explanation.surface: A figure: a small statuette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last L of DOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure or statue worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Slow bowler's skill beats leg

parts.note: to top is to beat or surpass
pin is informal for a leg

explanation.surface: A spinner's craft beats a leg-side batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg looks like cricket's leg side; here it is the informal 'pin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin bowlers in cricket impart forward rotation to the ball, a technique called topspin.

clue.text: Soldier feeding nothing to ginger tom

indicators.note: feeding one thing to another puts it inside, so this letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: a ginger tom is a red cat
O looks like zero, i.e. nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier gives his ginger cat no food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' puts O inside RED CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat was the name for a British soldier, from the scarlet uniform.

clue.text: Money in bank a few days ago?

indicators.note: in places the money piece within the other piece

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a coin, i.e. money

explanation.surface: Cash deposited at a bank lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a building for money; it is the verb meaning rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the last few days was done lately; the question mark admits the example.

clue.text: Killer in opening of silent film

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A murderer appears in the opening scene of a silent movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a coating, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A slayer is one who kills.
